T-002 ('Author resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1}'s evaluation pipeline (steps 0-13)') spans far more than three distinct implementation areas in one task: it authors three production scripts implementing 12+ distinct pipeline stages (argument validation, REQ-003 state derivation, workflow-combination validation, Project-Context canonicalization, Context Projection assembly, resolve-component-paths invocation, Registry discovery, per-Capability trigger evaluation, conditional-facet evaluation, the any-branch WARN check, the Full/Lite track branch and artifact staging, Resolver Evidence assembly, output-schema self-validation, and the pre-publication snapshot recheck), AND in the same task creates and registers five brand-new test suites with their own fixture trees (resolve-project-context-cli/-match/-lite/-discovery/-block, Planned Files list) covering twelve of REQ-002's sixteen Block diagnostics plus AC-001..AC-009/AC-016/AC-028/AC-038/AC-040/AC-041/AC-043/AC-044/AC-048/AC-052/AC-055/AC-056. This is not one coherent unit of work completable in a single focused session; by contrast T-003 and T-004 are each scoped to one cohesive mechanism. Recommend splitting T-002 so the core per-Capability evaluation/WARN/track-branch/Evidence-assembly logic is separable from its own CLI/discovery/lite-track suite authoring.

Functional tasks T-001/T-002/T-003/T-004 each carry extensive error-path/edge-case AC coverage beyond happy path: T-001's Done When requires fixtures per required-field-omission/wrong-type negative case (AC-018/AC-019); T-002 implements twelve of REQ-002's sixteen Block diagnostic rows (AC-010-AC-015) plus TOCTOU/staged-generation/aggregation edge cases (AC-038, AC-040, AC-041, AC-048, AC-052, AC-055, AC-056); T-003 implements the remaining four transactional Block diagnostics plus crash-recovery/rollback edge cases (AC-039, AC-047, AC-049); T-004 implements twelve provenance/structural check-ids plus two spoofing-attack provenance-binding fixture pairs (AC-050, AC-051) and a reader-side journal-check fixture (AC-054). No issues found.

This package uses a domain-specific contract-lock test-type vocabulary (e.g. 'required-flag matrix', 'discovery-contract reuse lock', 'union-match lock') rather than the generic unit/integration/e2e/acceptance taxonomy, applied consistently feature-wide. Every AC-NNN/TEST-NNN row in acceptance-tests.md maps 1:1 by row number with an explicit Test Target citing a concrete suite file and fixture, satisfying the 'must reference a specific AC-NNN' requirement for every row. Every test invokes the CLI against real or fixture-driven multi-subprocess dependencies (canonicalize-sdd-yaml, resolve-component-paths, evaluate-predicate, generate-registry-digest per design.md Architecture), consistent with cross-component scope; none is mislabeled as single-module-only while exercising the full pipeline. No issues found.

All three Risk: high tasks carry an explicit Rollback field: T-002 and T-003 each state 'revert this task's two commits (B then A, or both)' plus explicit guidance on hand-reverting an already-applied human-copy candidate on the protected path; T-004 states the same revert pattern and notes 'Nothing protected is touched'. infra-spec.md's own Rollback section additionally documents the runtime-level mechanism (journaled publication transaction / crash-recovery scan, T-003's own deliverable) as the actual data-level revert path. No issues found.

Every file touched by more than one task has its ordering enforced by an explicit Blockers/Depends-On chain and is named in tasks.md Global Constraints as a deliberate shared-scope case: resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1} is edited by exactly T-002 then T-003 (T-003 Blockers: T-002); tests/resolve-project-context-block.tests.sh/.ps1 is created by T-002 and appended-only by T-003; tests/run-all.sh/.ps1, the human-copy test.yml candidate, and human-copy/MANIFEST.sha256 are touched by T-001/T-002/T-004/T-005/T-006 in the declared serialized order, matching each task's own Blockers/Depends On edges. No two tasks claim to modify the same file for the same purpose without an enforcing Blockers relationship. No issues found.

Every Blockers/Depends On edge cites a concrete artifact dependency: T-002 on T-001 (step 12 schema self-validation needs T-001's schema); T-003 on T-002 (extends the same script; T-002's staged artifacts are T-003's transaction input); T-004 on T-001 (schema-invalid check) and T-003 (AC-054 needs a real TRANSACTION.json shape matching T-003's journal format); T-005/T-006 on T-002/T-003/T-004 (parity/metamorphic suites exercise the full pipeline plus validate-resolver-evidence's own triad). The six tasks form one strict topological chain (T-001->T-002->T-003->T-004->T-005/T-006), so no task's scope needs a blocker it lacks. No spurious or missing blockers found.
